page: The Microsoft Azure E20as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 20 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 10 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a 3.7 GHz clock frequency. It includes 160.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio designed for memory-intensive computations. This server type features hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no bundled local storage, requiring remote storage configurations for persistent disk needs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching top-quartile results in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core testing. In contrast, multi-core CPU evaluations such as Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU fall within the middle fifty percent. Memory bandwidth delivers 76.12 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 57.09 GB/sec for uncached writes, contributing to Redis SET throughput of 28.48 million operations per second. A performance tradeoff is evident in large-model artificial intelligence workloads, where prompt processing on 70B parameter models registers in the bottom twenty-five percent without GPU offloading.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the E20as_v6 is structured for workloads bounded by memory capacity rather than extreme multi-core scaling. The instance provides dedicated compute cores and high RAM density, preventing resource contention in memory-critical setups. Primary operational targets include in-memory databases, Redis cache deployments, mid-tier relational database engines, and structured data transformation pipelines.
